cítxʷsəlx uɬ t̓i nyʕ̓ip ck̓aʔítət iʔ smsámaʔ aʔ ct̓ʕapəntwíxʷ. uɬ ixíʔ scylyáltsəlx tl k̓ɬʔalqʷ. uɬ itlíʔ cxʷú·yəlx uɬ k̓t̓ət̓íw̓səlx uɬ nt̓ək̓ʷt̓ík̓ʷləx l nʔaysənúlaʔxʷ. uɬ ilíʔ nt̓ək̓ʷt̓ík̓ʷləx uɬ ixíʔ itlíʔ scxʷú·ysəlx nyʕ̓ip uɬ cxʷúyləx. uɬ cyáʕpəlx l Merritt l Godie, uɬ iʔ Sʔúl̓us mat ilíʔ t k̓ɬx̌ʷíləx t̓əxʷ mat. uɬ ixíʔ ilíʔ sk̓ʷul̓ ... k̓ʷl̓k̓ʷúl̓ɬxʷəmsəlx mat xʷəlxʷúl .... xʷəlxʷúlɬxʷəməlx ... k̓ʷl̓k̓ʷúl̓ɬxʷəməlx uɬ ilíʔ kʷlíwtləx. uɬ ixíʔ ʕapnáʔ iʔ sqilxʷ l Shulus uɬ l Godie Reserve, ya·ʕt taʔkín, ixíʔ iʔ sənk̓ʷúl̓tənsəlx, tl k̓ɬʔalqʷ kiʔ scxʷúyəlx. uɬ aláʔ cyá·ʕpəlx uɬ lut pənʔkín nixʷ sp̓lák̓səlx. kʷaʔ cmystísəlx way̓ ƛ̓axʷt iʔ sqəlqəltmíxʷ iʔ sənqsílxʷsəlx.

ƛ̓axʷt k̓l k̓ɬʔalqʷ uɬ cxʷúyləx aláʔ, uɬ itlíʔ Maggie Moore t tkɬmilxʷ. cnxíy̓ls iʔ ylyltmix, uɬ ckicx aláʔ uɬ ... tawsɬx̌ílwiʔ ... iʔ sx̌ílwiʔs, mat ilíʔ l təmxʷúlaʔxʷs. uɬ ilíʔ way̓ ƛ̓əx̌əx̌pwílx mat ixíʔ iʔ sqəltmíxʷ. uɬ k̓im Maggie t̓i sk̓ʷk̓ʷíyməlt pútiʔ uɬ k̓ʷu·l̓s uɬ ƛ̓lal iʔ ƛ̓əx̌ƛ̓x̌áp. uɬ cniɬc ilíʔ mut uɬ taʔlíʔ xʷaʔsqláw̓, nyʕ̓ip k̓ʷul̓s iʔ st̓mʕal̓t, iʔ nkɬc̓aʔsqáx̌aʔ. uɬ nyʕ̓i·p k̓ʷúl̓əm k̓ʷúl̓əm, uɬ pintk ʔaksqláw̓. uɬ k̓aʔít k̓íwəlx, lut nixʷ qɬnús ʔawsnmúləms iʔ tl cəcwíxaʔ, uɬ ksk̓ʷúl̓əms t kslip̓s. uɬ ixíʔ qʷəlqʷílsts mat ixíʔ sɬəɬw̓ílts naʔɬ Rosie naʔɬ ɬkíkxaʔs Rosie uɬ ixíʔ xʷíc̓ɬtəm August, cúntəm "kʷintxʷ August mi knxítəms." uɬ kʷənús August uɬ cnmúlxtəm, cknxítəm. uɬ cúntəm kʷukʷ iʔ t q̓ʷʕaylqs "way̓ ixíʔ ksʔawskúlaʔx" uɬ lut sxʔkínaʔs. lut x̌minks ksxʷuys August k̓l skul. uɬ qʷən̓kstmíst August. lut t̓a cmystis iʔ sq̓əy̓ám uɬ iʔ sread. uɬ k̓liʔ ƛ̓əx̌əx̌pwílx uɬ ƛ̓lal iʔ stəmtímaʔs uɬ siws nyʕ̓ip uɬ csəl̓mís iʔ .... síws nyʕ̓ip uɬ k̓aws iʔ st̓mʕal̓ts, k̓aws iʔ sqlaw̓s, k̓aws yaʕt stim̓ uɬ qʷən̓kstmíst sic mat cútləx t̓ʕapncút. kəm̓ mat t swit st̓ʕapám náx̌əmɬ ƛ̓lal. uɬ k̓ɬc̓sap ixíʔ sqlaw̓, lut stim̓ ilíʔ, uɬ ʕapnáʔ ixíʔ Margaret iʔ sqʷsiʔs t̓i n ilíʔ iʔ mut. uɬ ixíʔ aʔ ck̓ʷul̓s ixíʔ iʔ citxʷ, ixíʔ Maggie Moore iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷs. way̓.
q̓sápi ɬaʔ c-t̓ʕap-nwíxʷ kʷukʷ iʔ sm-sámaʔ iʔ naʔɬ sqilxʷ, ɬaʔ iʔ k̓l k̓ɬʔalqʷ.
‘A long time ago the whites and indians were shooting each other over across the line.’
uɬ ik̓líʔ c-yl-yalt [iʔ s] yaʕt iʔ s-qəl-qəltmíxʷ, kʷukʷ kʷín-(n)t-əm-əlx iʔ t government.
‘And all the men were running away, supposedly the government was taking them.’
uɬ ixíʔ s-t̓ʕap-nwíxʷ-əlx iʔ k̓l sm-sámaʔ uɬ k̓im t̓i kmax s-maʔ-mʔím uɬ pət-pə(p)twínaxʷ uɬ ƛ̓əx̌-əx̌-ƛ̓x̌áp, uɬ iʔ s-qʷsíʔ-aʔ-səlx.
‘And they were shooting each other (because of the white people) and there were only the women and old women and old men, and their children.’
uɬ kʷukʷ ixíʔ kʷlíwt-ləx iʔ l cítxʷ-səlx uɬ t̓i nyʕ̓ip c-k̓aʔít-ət iʔ sm-sámaʔ aʔ c-t̓ʕap-nwíxʷ.
‘And they supposedly lived in their houses and the whites were always getting closer, and they were shooting each other.’
uɬ ixíʔ s-c-yl-yált-səlx tl k̓ɬʔalqʷ.
‘And they ran from over the border.’
uɬ itlíʔ c-xʷú·y-əlx uɬ k̓t̓-ət̓-íw̓s-əlx uɬ n-t̓ək̓[ʷ]-t̓ík̓[ʷ]-ləx l nʔaysənúlaʔxʷ.
‘And they came so far, cut over the hill and they came down over at Ashnola.’
uɬ ilíʔ n-t̓ək̓[ʷ]-t̓ík̓[ʷ]-ləx uɬ ixíʔ itlíʔ s-c-xʷú·y-səlx nyʕ̓ip uɬ c-xʷúy-ləx.
‘And they traveled there and came from there.’
uɬ c-yáʕp-əlx l Merritt l Godie, uɬ iʔ s-ʔúl̓us mat ilíʔ t k̓ɬx̌ʷíl-(l)əx t̓əxʷ mat.
‘And they arrived just up above Merritt and at Godie reserve, and at Shulus. There must have been a lot of them.’
uɬ ixíʔ ilíʔ s-k̓ʷul̓ ... k̓ʷl̓-k̓ʷúl̓-ɬxʷ-əm-səlx mat xʷəl-xʷúl ... xʷəl-xʷúl-ɬxʷ-əm-əlx ... k̓ʷl̓-k̓ʷúl̓-ɬxʷ-əm-əlx uɬ ilíʔ kʷlíwt-ləx.
‘They made their homes there, made their tepees, and they lived there.’
uɬ ixíʔ ʕapnáʔ iʔ sqilxʷ l Shulus uɬ l Godie Reserve, ya·ʕt taʔkín, ixíʔ iʔ sən-k̓ʷúl̓-tən-səlx, tl k̓ɬʔalqʷ kiʔ s-c-xʷúy-əlx.
‘And the people there now, at Shulus and Godie Reserves, they built all over and used the land, and came from over the border.’
uɬ aláʔ c-yá·ʕp-əlx uɬ lut pənʔkín nixʷ s-p̓lák̓-səlx.
‘Once they got here they never went back again.’
kʷaʔ c-my-st-ísəlx way̓ ƛ̓axʷt iʔ s-qəl-qəltmíxʷ iʔ s-nqs-ílxʷ-səlx.
‘Because they knew that their men-relatives must have gotten killed.’
ƛ̓axʷt k̓l k̓ɬʔalqʷ uɬ c-xʷúy-ləx aláʔ, uɬ itlíʔ Maggie Moore t tkɬmilxʷ.
‘They died over the border, and came here, and that’s where Maggie Moore came from.’
c-nxíy̓ls iʔ yl-ylt-mix, uɬ c-kic-x aláʔ uɬ ... taws-ɬ-x̌ílwiʔ ... iʔ s-x̌ílwiʔ-s, mat ilíʔ l təmxʷúlaʔxʷ-s.
‘All the ones that ran away mixed among others and arrived here. She (Maggie) got with her husband, who owned the land.’
uɬ ilíʔ way̓ ƛ̓əx̌-əx̌-p-wílx mat ixíʔ iʔ sqəltmíxʷ.
‘And he was an older man.’
uɬ k̓im Maggie t̓i s-k̓ʷ-k̓ʷíy-m-əlt pútiʔ uɬ k̓ʷu·l̓-s uɬ ƛ̓lal iʔ ƛ̓əx̌-ƛ̓x̌áp.
‘And Maggie was young yet, and she looked after him until he died.’
uɬ cniɬc ilíʔ mut uɬ taʔlíʔ xʷaʔ-sqláw̓, nyʕ̓ip k̓ʷul̓-s iʔ st̓mʕal̓t, iʔ (sə)nkɬc̓aʔsqáx̌aʔ.
‘And she lived there and always had lots of money and worked hard, had lots of cattle and horses.’
uɬ nyʕ̓i·p k̓ʷúl̓-əm k̓ʷúl̓-əm, uɬ pintk ʔak(ɬ)-sqláw̓.
‘And she was always working, working, and had lots of money.’
uɬ k̓aʔít k̓íw-əlx, lut nixʷ qɬ-nú-s [ks-n-] ... ʔaws-n-múl-əm-s iʔ tl cə-cwíxaʔ, uɬ ks-k̓ʷúl̓-əm-s t k(ɬ)-slip̓-s.
‘Then she got older and she couldn’t pack water from the creek, or pack wood.’
uɬ ixíʔ qʷəl-qʷíl-st-s mat ixíʔ sɬəɬw̓ílt-s [kʷaʔɬ] naʔɬ Rosie naʔɬ ɬkíkxaʔ-s Rosie uɬ ixíʔ xʷíc̓-ɬt-əm August, cún-(n)t-əm “kʷin-(n)t-xʷ August mi kn-xít-əm-s.”
‘And she talked to her niece and Rosie and Rosie’s older sister, and she gave her (Maggie) August, she told Maggie “Take August, he will help you.”’
uɬ kʷə(n)-nú-s August uɬ c-n-múl-xt-əm, c-kn-xít-əm.
‘And she took August, and he packed water, he packed wood.’
uɬ cún-(n)t-əm kʷukʷ iʔ t q̓ʷʕay-lqs “way̓ ixíʔ ks-ʔaws-(s)kúl-aʔx” uɬ lut sxʔ(k)ínaʔ-s.
‘And the priest told her “He has to go to school”, but she didn’t want him to go.’
lut x̌mink-s ks-xʷuy-s August k̓l skul. uɬ qʷən̓-kst-míst August.
‘She didn’t want August to go to school, and August felt bad.’
lut t̓a c-my-st-is iʔ s-q̓əy̓-ám uɬ iʔ s-read.
‘He didn’t know how to write or read.’
uɬ k̓liʔ ƛ̓əx̌-əx̌-p-wílx uɬ ƛ̓lal iʔ stəmtímaʔ-s uɬ siw-s nyʕ̓ip uɬ c-səl̓-mí-s iʔ ....
‘And his grandmother got old and died, and he drank all the time and lost the....’
síw-s nyʕ̓ip uɬ k̓aw-s iʔ st̓mʕal̓t-s, k̓aw-s iʔ sqlaw̓-s, k̓aw-s yaʕt stim̓ uɬ qʷən̓-kst-míst sic mat cút-ləx t̓ʕap-ncút.
‘He drank all the time and lost his cattle, lost his money, lost everything and felt bad until, they say, he shot himself.’
kəm̓ mat t swit s-t̓ʕap-ám náx̌əmɬ ƛ̓lal.
‘Or maybe somebody shot him, but in any case, he died.’
uɬ k̓ɬc̓sap ixíʔ sqlaw̓, lut stim̓ ilíʔ, uɬ ʕapnáʔ ixíʔ Margaret iʔ sqʷsiʔ-s t̓i [n] ilíʔ iʔ mut.
‘They spent all the money, nothing was left there, Margaret’s son is the one living there now.’
uɬ ixíʔ aʔ c-k̓ʷul̓-s ixíʔ iʔ citxʷ, ixíʔ Maggie Moore iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷ-s. way̓.
‘And where he built that house, that’s Maggie Moore’s land. That’s all.’
(a)laʔ

form: They came from across the line. The [U.S.] government took the men and made them go to the war. They were fighting towards the border, and the women and children ran away over the border. They were getting closer and they ran away and they came out around Ashnola, and from there they came straight to the Nicola Valley. They came so far. They cut over the hill and came down around Ashnola, just up above Merritt, on the way to Princeton. They made their homes there in Shulus and Godie reserve, going towards Vancouver. The tepees and whatever they had to make their homes with, they built homes and they lived there. They built all over, they used the land. Once they got here they never went back again. Because the men never showed up anywhere, so they knew they must’ve been killed. That’s where Maggie Moore came from, one of those people. All the ones that ran away, they mixed among others. She got with her husband. Her husband owned the land. He was older. She was young yet, and she looked after him until he died, and then everything was hers. And she always had lots of money and worked hard, had lots of cattle and horses. Then she got older and she couldn’t pack water. She couldn’t pack wood, but she talked to her niece. Annie’s son, August, Annie was another niece, Rosie didn’t have children. He stayed with this old lady, she didn’t speak English herself, she wouldn’t let him go to the school. He [August] packed water, he packed wood. The priest talked to her and she didn’t want him to go [to school]. August felt bad. People said he shot himself, but in any case, he died. They finished everything, nothing but wrecked cars, they spent all the money. Margaret’s son Dean is the one living there now. Where Dean’s house is is Maggie Moore’s property.
McIntyre Bluff
gloss: roughly halfway between Skaha and Osoyoos Lakes, where the story takes place

form: q̓sápi kʷukʷ iʔ sqilxʷ ɬaʔ ctyaqʷt. tyaqʷts iʔ syilx, uɬ iʔ syxʷápməx, uɬ kʷukʷ ixíʔ ɬaʔ ckilənwíxʷəlx, məɬ qíxʷsəlx məɬ qíxʷəntəməlx. uɬ xʷúyəlx kʷukʷ uɬ k̓l k̓ɬʔalqʷ, k̓ík̓əm ksyáʕpsəlx k̓l k̓ɬʔalqʷ, kaʔkín mat k̓l k̓aʔítətləx k̓liʔ. uɬ kʷukʷ ixíʔ sxʷúyʔsəlx k̓ɬx̌ʷil, k̓ɬx̌ʷil kʷukʷ iʔ sxʷúyʔsəlx uɬ l təɬtíɬx l wist uɬ ilíʔ kʷukʷ uɬ yaʕyáʕt səʕsáʕtləx. səʕsáʕtləx uɬ taɬt k̓l qʷəmí··w̓t kiw̓ mat kiʔ yaʕt ƛ̓áxʷtləx. uɬ k̓im kʷukʷ t̓i knaqs t ƛ̓əx̌ƛ̓x̌áp act̓kíkst, uɬ kʷukʷ ixíʔ, iʔ t t̓kíkstəns kaʔ cxʷuy. nyʕ̓ip wtəntís iʔ t̓kíkstəns uɬ cmystis kʷukʷ xʷuy uɬ mynús, lut, way̓ t̓i ak̓láʔ xərxárt, uɬ nwíwpəm. uɬ ixíʔ ilíʔ sƛ̓laps. uɬ mat t swit t̓əxʷ kiʔ kaʔkícəntəm, uɬ cúntəm kʷukʷ “ƛ̓axʷt yaʕyáʕt asənqsílxʷ, k̓laʔ səʕsáʕtləx.” uɬ ixíʔ ɬaʔ ck̓sax̌təmnwíxʷ iʔ syilx naʔɬ syxʷápməx. uɬ səʕsáʕt iʔ sl̓əx̌l̓áx̌tsəlx uɬ kmax aʔ cknəmqín aʔ cxʷəlxʷált. uɬ ixíʔ itlíʔ kʷukʷ p̓əlk̓stísəlx, uɬ c̓sap iʔ sənqsílxʷs uɬ ixíʔ itlíʔ kʷísəlx, xʷúysəlx, uɬ cxʷəlxʷált cniɬc k̓im ƛ̓axʷt iʔ k̓ʷiƛ̓t. uɬ ixíʔ q̓sápi kʷukʷ ɬaʔ ck̓liʔ kʷu cxʷuy iʔ k̓l Keremeos, xʷúystəm Matilda. Matilda Chillhitzia xʷúystəm. uɬ ixíʔ kʷu cm̓ayxítəm. kʷu cm̓ayxítəm kʷu cxʷuy, uɬ iʔ kʷu cus "axáʔ aláʔ cmystikʷ, axáʔ aláʔ nq̓aʔmw̓scút." ilíʔ kʷukʷ kaʔ cwíkʷəmist iʔ syilx, sƛ̓aʔƛ̓aʔstím iʔ t syxʷápməx kspúlstəm uɬ ilíʔ nq̓aʔmw̓scút ɬaʔ cnsq̓iw̓s iʔ l xƛ̓ut. uɬ lut kaʔkíciʔsəlx uɬ lut púlstsəlx. ixíʔ kʷu m̓ayxíts Matilda ɬaʔ ctytyaqʷt iʔ sqilxʷ q̓sápi. uɬ kʷukʷ itlíʔ cxʷuy uɬ cxʷuy məɬ alaʔ ɬcyáʕpəlx l zuxʷt kəm̓ mat k̓əɬáʔ k̓l shulus. uɬ sylyáltləx. uɬ nyʕ̓ip ilíʔ ʔx̌íləməlx itíʔ nyʕ̓ip tyáqʷtləx. uɬ yrmíntəməlx iʔ t syilx, uɬ yrmíntəməlx uɬ k̓l Stump Lake. uɬ itlíʔ iʔ səmúlaʔxʷ ʕapnáʔ. úɬiʔ náx̌əmɬ ilíʔ kiʔ ƛ̓lap, uɬ ck̓laʔ mnímɬtət. kʷlnúntəm iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷ, kʷanúntəm. uɬ ixíʔ ʕapnáʔ iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷtət, ƛ̓xʷúpəntəm iʔ tl syxʷápməx. ƛ̓xʷəntísəlx mat iʔ xʷʔit iʔ syxʷápməx, uɬ ƛ̓xʷúpsəlx ixíʔ iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷ. scʔx̌iɬx kiʔ aláʔ iʔ kʷu kʷliwt, kʷu syilx. kʷaʔ lut aláʔ t̓ ʔaksyilx, k̓laʔ syxʷápməx k̓l Kamloops, uɬ tac k̓l Merritt, nuk̓ʷtmíxʷ. k̓im axáʔ aláʔ kʷu k̓ʷək̓ʷyúmaʔ t syilx, t sqilxʷ, uɬ aláʔ kʷu kʷliwt. kʷaʔ ƛ̓xʷúpəntəm ixíʔ ɬaʔ ctyaqʷt iʔ sənxaʔcínəmtət iʔ xəʔxʔítət, ɬaʔ ctyáqʷtləx uɬ ixíʔ ƛ̓xʷúpsəlx. uɬ scʔx̌iɬx kiʔ aláʔ iʔ kʷu kʷliwt, iʔ kʷu sqilxʷ. uɬ k̓im iʔ syxʷápməx yaʕyáʕt tl xʷúyəlx mat. uɬ ixíʔ ya·ʕt kʷu m̓ayɬtím Matilda taʔkín kaʔ cpúlxəlx, taʔkín kaʔ cwkʷwíkʷmistləx, ɬaʔ ctytyáqʷtləx. uɬ ɬaʔ cxʷəlxʷált Herbie, kʷu cus “ixíʔ ksk̓ɬʔíysəntəm iʔ skʷstúlaʔxʷ, kʷaʔ yaʔx̌ís skʷstúlaʔxʷ yaʕyáʕt syxʷápməx, syxʷápməx iʔ skʷstúlaʔxʷs.” uɬ t Herbie cut “ixíʔ kskʷísəntəm t nqʷəlqʷíltəntət.”

uɬ cun “lut, ciʔskʷ ilíʔ way̓ t̓i iʔ scʔx̌iɬx, way̓ ixíʔ sƛ̓xʷúptət. uɬ ixíʔ n̓ín̓w̓iʔs ɬ mypnús swit l syxʷpmxúlaʔxʷs.” “n̓ín̓w̓iʔs mi ... itlíʔ mi ƛ̓xʷúpəntəm. k̓im k̓ɬʔí·ysənt uɬ cmay səl̓míntəm.” uɬ kʷu cus “way̓ m̓ayɬtín stim̓ iʔ kʷu m̓ayxíts isw̓aw̓ásaʔ.” uɬ kʷu cus “way̓ x̌ast, lut ksk̓ɬʔíysəntəm.” uɬ yaʕyáʕt ixíʔ Sharon x̌minks kʷu ksíwəntəm, yaʕt iʔ t skʷskʷstúlaʔxʷ, mi n̓ín̓w̓iʔs ixíʔ cúɬtəm ɬaʔ cmystim. ixíʔ iʔ stqʷəlíplaʔs, ixíʔ kiʔ aláʔ iʔ kʷu sqilxʷ iʔ kʷu k̓ʷək̓ʷíynaʔt iʔ t sqilxʷ, t syilx. ixíʔ iʔ sƛ̓xʷups iʔ ƛ̓əx̌əx̌ƛ̓x̌áp iʔ sənxaʔcínəmtət ɬaʔ ctyáqʷtləx, kiʔ aláʔ kʷu kʷliwt. uɬ cakʷ taʔlí··ʔ cx̌aʔstím, cakʷ taʔlíʔ cx̌síkstəmstəm ʕant aláʔ iʔ sx̌ástət ʕapnáʔ. l nkʷr̓itkʷ kiʔ kʷu kʷliwt, x̌ast iʔ spuʔústət, x̌ast iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷ. cakʷ lut iʔ ƛ̓əx̌əx̌ƛ̓x̌áptət, cakʷ ixíʔ səl̓míntəm, cakʷ aláʔ iʔ smsámaʔ kiʔ kʷliwt ʕapnáʔ. ixíʔ iʔ sm̓ym̓ays axáʔ iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷtət kiʔ aláʔ kʷu kʷliwt. way̓.
q̓sápi kʷukʷ iʔ sqilxʷ ɬaʔ c-tyaqʷt.
‘Long ago, they say the people were fighting.’
tyaqʷt-s iʔ syilx, uɬ iʔ syxʷáp-məx, uɬ kʷukʷ ixíʔ ɬaʔ c-kil-nwíxʷ-əlx, məɬ qíxʷ-səlx məɬ qíxʷ-nt-əm-əlx.
‘The Okanagans fought the Shuswaps, and they say they chased one another, back and forth.’
uɬ xʷúy-əlx kʷukʷ uɬ k̓l k̓ɬʔalqʷ, k̓ík̓əm ks-yáʕp-səlx k̓l k̓ɬʔalqʷ, kaʔkín mat k̓l k̓aʔít-ət-ləx k̓liʔ.
‘And they went to the border, they almost got to the border, wherever they got close to there.’
uɬ kʷukʷ ixíʔ s-xʷúyʔ-səlx k̓ɬx̌ʷil, k̓ɬx̌ʷil kʷukʷ iʔ s-xʷúyʔ-səlx uɬ l təɬ-tíɬx l wist uɬ ilíʔ kʷukʷ uɬ yaʕyáʕt səʕ-sáʕt-ləx.
‘And they say that there were lots of them that went right on top of a high mountain, and then they all fell over the edge.’
səʕ-sáʕt-ləx uɬ taɬt k̓l qʷəmí··w̓t kiw̓ mat kiʔ yaʕt ƛ̓áxʷt-ləx.
‘They fell off straight off the top and they must’ve all died.’
uɬ k̓im kʷukʷ t̓i knaqs t ƛ̓əx̌-ƛ̓x̌áp ac-t̓k-íkst, uɬ kʷukʷ ixíʔ, iʔ t t̓k-íks(t)-tən-s kaʔ c-xʷuy.
‘And there was one old man with a cane, and they say that it was him, with a cane, that came.’
nyʕ̓ip wt-nt-ís iʔ t̓k-íks(t)-tən-s uɬ c-my-st-is kʷukʷ xʷuy uɬ my-nú-s, lut, way̓ t̓i ak̓láʔ xər-xárt, uɬ n-wí-wp-əm.
‘He always had a cane ahead of him, and knew where he was going, and he felt that there was a steep edge there, and he backed up.’
uɬ ixíʔ (i)líʔ s-ƛ̓lap-s.
‘And he stopped there.’
uɬ mat t swit t̓əxʷ kiʔ kaʔkíc-nt-əm, uɬ cún-(n)t-əm kʷukʷ “ƛ̓axʷt yaʕyáʕt a(n)-s-nqs-ílxʷ, k̓laʔ səʕ-sáʕt-ləx.”
‘And somebody must have found him, and told him “All your people are dead, they fell off a cliff.”’
uɬ ixíʔ ɬaʔ c-k̓s-ax̌t-m(n)-nwíxʷ iʔ syilx naʔɬ syxʷáp-məx.
‘And the Okanagans and Shuswaps were pushing and threatening one another.’
uɬ səʕ-sáʕt iʔ s-l̓əx̌-l̓áx̌t-səlx uɬ kmax aʔ c-knəmqín aʔ c-xʷəl-xʷált.
‘And all their friends fell off, and there was just one blind man left alive.’
uɬ ixíʔ itlíʔ kʷukʷ p̓əlk̓-st-ísəlx, uɬ c̓sap iʔ s-nqs-ílxʷ-s uɬ ixíʔ itlíʔ kʷí(n)-səlx, xʷúy-səlx, uɬ c-xʷəl-xʷált cniɬc k̓im ƛ̓axʷt iʔ k̓ʷiƛ̓t.
‘And they took him back to their place, all his relatives were gone, and they took him and brought him, and he stayed alive while the others died.’
uɬ ixíʔ q̓sápi kʷukʷ ɬaʔ c-k̓liʔ kʷu c-xʷuy iʔ k̓l Keremeos, xʷúy-st-əm Matilda.
‘And that’s what happened long ago over there; we came to Keremeos, we drove Matilda there.’
Matilda Chillhitzia xʷúy-st-əm. uɬ ixíʔ kʷu c-m̓ay-xít-əm. kʷu c-m̓ay-xít-əm kʷu c-xʷuy, uɬ iʔ kʷu cu-s “axáʔ aláʔ c-my-st-ikʷ, axáʔ aláʔ n-q̓aʔm-w̓s-cút.”
‘We drove Matilda Chillhitzia, and she told us the story, and told us “Know this! Here in between the rocks, and they survived.”’
ilíʔ kʷukʷ kaʔ c-wíkʷ-mist iʔ syilx, s-ƛ̓aʔ-ƛ̓aʔ-st-ím iʔ t syxʷáp-məx ks-púl-st-əm uɬ ilíʔ n-q̓aʔm-w̓s-cút ɬaʔ c-n-sq̓-iw̓s iʔ l xƛ̓ut.
‘And they say the Okanagans hid in there, the Shuswaps looked for them to kill them, and they survived by hiding in the split rock.’
uɬ lut kaʔkíc-isəlx uɬ lut púl-st-səlx.
‘And they didn’t find them, and they didn’t kill them.’
ixíʔ kʷu m̓ay-xít-s Matilda ɬaʔ c-ty-tyaqʷt iʔ sqilxʷ q̓sápi.
‘Matilda told me that story about the people fighting long ago.’
uɬ kʷukʷ itlíʔ c-xʷuy uɬ c-xʷuy məɬ alaʔ ɬ-c-yáʕp-əlx l zuxʷt kəm̓ mat k̓əɬáʔ k̓l shulus.
‘And they got back here, maybe in Nicola or maybe this way to Shulus.’
uɬ s-yl-yált-ləx. uɬ nyʕ̓ip ilíʔ ʔx̌íl-əm-əlx itíʔ nyʕ̓ip tyáqʷt-ləx.
‘And they all ran away. And they were always doing like that, fighting all the time.’
uɬ yr-mín-(n)t-əm-əlx iʔ t syilx, uɬ yr-mín-(n)t-əm-əlx uɬ k̓l Stump Lake.
‘And they (the Shuswaps) were pushed, pushed over to Stump Lake.’
uɬ itlíʔ iʔ səm-úlaʔxʷ ʕapnáʔ.
‘And today it’s government land.’
úɬiʔ náx̌əmɬ ilíʔ kiʔ ƛ̓lap, uɬ c-k̓laʔ mnímɬtət.
‘That’s where they stopped. And we’re here.’
kʷl-nún-(n)t-əm iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷ, kʷa(n)-nún-(n)t-əm.
‘We settled on the land, we got the land.’
uɬ ixíʔ ʕapnáʔ iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷ-tət, ƛ̓xʷúp-nt-əm iʔ tl syxʷáp-məx.
‘And now it’s our land, we won it from the Shuswaps.’
ƛ̓xʷ-nt-ísəlx mat iʔ xʷʔit iʔ syxʷáp-məx, uɬ ƛ̓xʷúp-səlx ixíʔ iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷ.
‘They killed lots of Shuswaps, and they won this land.’
scʔx̌iɬx kiʔ aláʔ iʔ kʷu kʷliwt, kʷu syilx.
‘That’s why we’re living here, us Okanagans.’
kʷaʔ lut aláʔ t̓ ʔak(ɬ)-syílx, k̓laʔ syxʷáp-məx k̓l Kamloops, uɬ tac k̓l Merritt, nuk̓ʷtmíxʷ.
‘And there’s no Okanagans, just Shuswaps, towards Kamloops, and towards Merritt, the Thompson.’
k̓im axáʔ aláʔ kʷu k̓ʷə-k̓ʷyúmaʔ t syilx, t sqilxʷ, uɬ aláʔ kʷu kʷliwt.
‘We’re just small Syilx people here, but here we’re living.’
kʷaʔ ƛ̓xʷúp-nt-əm ixíʔ ɬaʔ c-tyaqʷt iʔ sənxaʔcínəm-tət iʔ xəʔ-xʔít-(t)ət, ɬaʔ c-tyáqʷt-ləx uɬ ixíʔ ƛ̓xʷúp-səlx.
‘Because our leaders, our parents, the people ahead of us, our ancestors, they fought and they won.’
uɬ scʔx̌iɬx kiʔ aláʔ iʔ kʷu kʷliwt, iʔ kʷu sqilxʷ.
‘And that’s why we’re living here, us Okanagans.’
uɬ k̓im iʔ syxʷáp-məx yaʕyáʕt tl xʷúy-əlx mat.
‘All the Shuswaps went home.’
uɬ ixíʔ ya·ʕt kʷu m̓ay-ɬt-ím Matilda taʔkín kaʔ c-púlx-əlx, taʔkín kaʔ c-wkʷ-wíkʷ-mist-ləx, ɬaʔ c-ty-tyáqʷt-ləx.
‘And Matilda told us everything about where they were camping, where they were hiding when they were fighting.’
uɬ ɬaʔ c-xʷəl-xʷált Herbie, kʷu cu-s “ixíʔ ks-k̓ɬʔíys-nt-əm iʔ skʷst-úlaʔxʷ, kʷaʔ yaʔx̌ís skʷst-úlaʔxʷ yaʕyáʕt syxʷáp-məx, syxʷáp-məx iʔ skʷst-úlaʔxʷ-s.”
‘And when Herbie was alive, he told me “We should change the names of the places because they’re all Shuswap names.”’
uɬ t Herbie cut “ixíʔ ks-kʷís-nt-əm t n-qʷəl-qʷíl-tən-tət.”
‘And Herbie said “Let’s rename them to our language.”’
uɬ cu-n “lut, ciʔ-skʷ ilíʔ way̓ t̓i iʔ scʔx̌iɬx, way̓ ixíʔ s-ƛ̓xʷúp-tət. uɬ ixíʔ n̓ín̓w̓iʔs ɬ my-p-nú-s swit l syxʷp-mx-úlaʔxʷ-s.”
‘And I told him “No, leave it alone, like it is now. We won the land, and maybe someday someone will need to know it was Shuswap land.”’
“n̓ín̓w̓iʔs mi ... itlíʔ mi ƛ̓xʷúp-nt-əm. k̓im k̓ɬʔi·ys-nt uɬ cmay səl̓-mín-(n)t-əm.”
‘“That’s how we won it over, if we change it we might lose it.”’
uɬ kʷu cu-s “way̓ m̓ay-ɬt-ín stim̓ iʔ kʷu m̓ay-xít-s i(n)-sw̓aw̓ásaʔ.”
‘And he told me “Yes, I told you what my aunt told me.”’
uɬ kʷu cu-s “way̓ x̌ast, lut ks-k̓ɬʔíys-nt-əm.”
‘And he told me “Okay, we won’t change it.”’
uɬ yaʕyáʕt ixíʔ Sharon x̌mink-s kʷu k(s)-síw-nt-əm, yaʕt iʔ t s-kʷs-kʷst-úlaʔxʷ, mi n̓ín̓w̓iʔs ixíʔ cú(n)-ɬt-əm ɬaʔ c-my-st-im.
‘And everything Sharon wants to ask us about, all the place names, we can tell her what we know.’
ixíʔ iʔ s-t-qʷəl-íplaʔ-s, ixíʔ kiʔ aláʔ iʔ kʷu sqilxʷ iʔ kʷu k̓ʷə-k̓ʷíynaʔt iʔ t sqilxʷ, t syilx.
‘That’s what we’re talking about, how we got to be here, us few Native people, Okanagan people.’
ixíʔ iʔ s-ƛ̓xʷup-s iʔ ƛ̓əx̌-əx̌-ƛ̓x̌áp iʔ sənxaʔcínəm-tət ɬaʔ c-tyáqʷt-ləx, kiʔ aláʔ kʷu kʷliwt.
‘Our elders, those that came ahead of us, they fought and won it over for us, that’s why we are here.’
uɬ cakʷ taʔlí··ʔ c-x̌aʔ-st-ím, cakʷ taʔlíʔ c-x̌s-íkst-əm-st-əm ʕant aláʔ iʔ s-x̌ás-tət ʕapnáʔ.
‘We should really treat it well, really take care of it, so that it’s the way we want.’
l n-kʷr̓-itkʷ kiʔ kʷu kʷliwt, x̌ast iʔ s-puʔús-tət, x̌ast iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷ.
‘At Glimpse Lake where we’re staying, we really like it, the land is good.’
cakʷ lut iʔ ƛ̓əx̌-əx̌-ƛ̓x̌áp-tət, cakʷ ixíʔ səl̓-mín-(n)t-əm, cakʷ aláʔ iʔ sm-sámaʔ kiʔ kʷliwt ʕapnáʔ.
‘If it wasn’t for our ancestors we might have lost it, and the whites might have been living here instead.’
ixíʔ iʔ s-m̓y-m̓ay-s axáʔ iʔ təmxʷúlaʔxʷ-tət kiʔ aláʔ kʷu kʷliwt. way̓.
‘That’s my story about this land and how we came to live here. That’s all.’

form: A long time ago the people were fighting one another. They were chasing one another, they’d chase them so far, kinda back and forth. And getting close to the border, where the bluff is near Oliver, almost got to the border. And right up on top of the mountain, it was steep and night time on the high mountain, they all fell over, way down on the river, they all must have died. Except for one old blind man with the cane, who survived. He always had a cane ahead of him, and he felt that there was an edge there. It’s steep there, and he backed up. He stopped. And he probably called for them and no answer, he just stayed there, until the next day somebody went to look where all those people fell over, and he was sitting there. Somebody found him. “All your people are dead, they fell off of a cliff.” They were pushing and threatening one another. There was just one blind man left alive. And they rescued him and took him with those people that were living around Oliver. They took him back to their place. His relatives were all gone. He was alive and all the rest died. We drove Matilda to a funeral and she was telling us the spots where people were dying, there’s a place they call “the hanging place” because somebody hung themselves there. That’s how I know because she told me the story about when the people were fighting. ‘In between the rocks’, ‘split rock’, and they survived, on the way to Princeton that way where the rest fell over, they stayed up in the hills. The Okanagans hid in there. The Shuswaps were looking for them and ‘split rock’ was where he hid. And they didn’t find him and they didn’t kill him. Matilda told that story long ago, what happened. Then they got here. Maybe in Nicola or Shulus, or in Merritt they said there was a big camp place there where NVIT is. They were fighting all the time. So the Okanagans pushed the Shuswaps down towards Kamloops, now it’s government land. That’s where they stopped. We got the land, Okanagans were all over, and from there they came up here to be Keepers of the Land. That’s why we’re here as Syilx people, Syilx. Kamloops was the Shuswap and towards Shulus was the Thompson. We’re just small Syilx people here. We won the land because of our leaders, our parents, the people ahead of us, ancestors. That’s why we’re here. All the Shuswaps went home, that was the end of the fight. And Matilda told me about where they were hiding when they were fighting. Mother and Father’s background was from down south, so my father’s from 100 Mile House, and never did go back. And while Herbie was still alive he said “Let’s rename the Shuswap names to Okanagan names.” I said to leave it alone. That’s how we won it over, it’ll show how we won it over, by not changing the names of the places. Whoever is measuring the land will need to know someday. My aunt told me the story, so we won’t change it. We can tell Sharon all the names that she wants to know. What we’re doing through Sharon, we can tell the story, we can talk about it. Our elders ahead of us, they won it over for us, that’s why we’re here. We should really look after it, the people suffered who were here. We should look after it because this is where we live. The place is nice. If it wasn’t for our ancestors we might have lost it, we could have lost it. Sámaʔs would’ve been there and maybe made something out of it.
